subject.title: Feature: Postcondition checks for cron jobs (deterministic verification of agent outcomes)

question: Should cron post-run verification be implemented as a scheduler-owned bounded verifier contract, a fail-capable plugin hook, or deferred until a broader agent outcome-verification API exists?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the proposed capability changes public cron config/protocol/state and can execute unattended checks with run/session context, so automation should not choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Approve bounded scheduler contract
options.body: Define typed post-run verification owned by cron, with explicit command/plugin adapters, timeout/output/redaction rules, persisted status, retry limits, and failure-alert integration.

options.title: Add plugin seam first
options.body: Expose a fail-capable cron post-run hook that can return pass, fail, retry, or escalate decisions while verifier implementation remains outside core.

options.title: Defer verifier API
options.body: Keep this issue as the specific design tracker until maintainers settle broader outcome-verification semantics across cron and outbound hooks.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded scheduler contract
recommendation.body: Define typed post-run verification owned by cron, with explicit command/plugin adapters, timeout/output/redaction rules, persisted status, retry limits, and failure-alert integration.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combination of official ownership, prior issue review, and recent source history across the affected cron runtime and protocol surfaces.
